subject: maths
title: Counting to 100: One More, One Less and Numbers in Words
seo_title: Year 1 Counting to 100 Worksheets: One More and One Less, Number Words to 20
standard_text: Count to and across 100, forwards and backwards, beginning with 0 or 1, or from any given number; count, read and write numbers to 100 in numerals; given a number, identify one more and one less; identify and represent numbers using objects and pictorial representations including the number line, and use the language of: equal to, more than, less than (fewer), most, least; read and write numbers from 1 to 20 in numerals and words.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 counting to 100 maths worksheets for the National Curriculum: count objects, numbers to 20 in words, one more and one less, counting across tens on a hundred square, and more, less, most and least. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Touch each thing once and say one number for each. After 9 ones comes a new ten: 29, 30.
key_sub: One more is the next number. One less is the number just before: one less than 40 is 39. Twelve is written 12, not 21.
body_html:
Counting means saying the numbers in order

Say one number for each thing. Touch each thing once. The last number you say is how many.

Put things in rows of 10 (5 and 5). Then you do not lose your place.

Numbers to 20 in words

NumberWordNumberWord
11eleven16sixteen
12twelve17seventeen
13thirteen18eighteen
14fourteen19nineteen
15fifteen20twenty

Teen numbers are 10 and some more. Thirteen is 13. Thirty is 30.

One more and one less

One more is the next number. One less is the number just before.

One less

What is one less than 40?

Count back 1: 40, 39. You only go back one step.

Answer: 39 (not 49 or 30)

The hundred square

Each row has 10 numbers. Go right for one more. Go down for ten more.

More, less, most and least

Look at the tens first. 41 has 4 tens. 36 has 3 tens. So 41 is more than 36.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 12 as 21Twelve is 10 and 2. The 1 comes first: 12
Mixing up thirteen and thirtyThirteen is 13. Thirty is 30
Writing 310 after 399 ones and 1 more make a new ten: 40
One less than 40 is 49 or 30Count back just one: 39
Counting a thing twiceTouch each thing once, or put them in rows

faq.q: What maths does a Year 1 child learn?
faq.a: Year 1 children count to 100, read and write numbers to 20 in words, and add and subtract within 20. They also learn halves and quarters, money, time, length and shapes.

faq.q: How high should a Year 1 child count?
faq.a: By the end of Year 1, children should count to 100, forwards and backwards, starting from any number. They should also give one more and one less than a number.

faq.q: Why does my child write 21 for twelve?
faq.a: Twelve sounds like it starts with the 2. Show twelve as 10 and 2 more with counters, then write the 1 for the ten first: 12.

faq.q: How can I help my child count to 100 at home?
faq.a: Count real things like steps, stairs and toys, and point at a hundred square as you say the numbers. Practise the tricky parts, such as 29, 30 and 40, 39.

items.q: How many apples?
items.e: Touch each one once: 1, 2, 3, 4. There are 4 apples.
Touch each one once. The first 5, then count on: 6, 7. There are 7 stars.

items.q: How many balls?
items.e: Touch each one once. The first 5, then count on: 6, 7, 8, 9. There are 9 balls.
Touch each one once. The first 5, then count on: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. There are 10 buttons.

items.q: Which number is “twelve”?
items.e: Twelve is 10 and 2 more. Write 12. 21 is twenty-one.

items.q: How many apples?
items.e: The top row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12. There are 12 apples.
The top row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13. There are 13 stars.

items.q: Which number is “thirteen”?
items.e: Thirteen is 10 and 3 more. Write 13. Thirty is 30.

items.q: How many counters? Choose the word.
items.e: The first frame is full: 10. Then 1 more: 11. Say eleven.

items.q: How many balls?
items.e: The top row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. There are 15 balls.
The top row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. There are 16 buttons.

items.q: Which number is “fifteen”?
items.e: Fifteen is 10 and 5 more. Write 15. Fifty is 50.

items.q: How many counters? Choose the word.
items.e: 10 and 4 more is 14. Say fourteen. Forty is 40.

items.q: How many apples?
items.e: The top row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18. There are 18 apples.
The top row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14. There are 14 buttons.

items.q: Which number is “seventeen”?
items.e: Seventeen is 10 and 7 more. Write 17. Seventy is 70.

items.q: How many counters? Choose the word.
items.e: 10 and 9 more is 19. Say nineteen. Ninety is 90.

items.q: How many balls?
items.e: The top row has 10. Then count on: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. There are 17 balls.
Each full row has 10. 10, 20. There are 20 stars.

items.q: How many counters? Choose the word.
items.e: Both frames are full: 10 and 10 is 20. Say twenty. Twelve is 12.

items.q: What is one more than 6?
items.e: Count on 1: 6, 7. Only the ones digit changes.

items.q: What is one less than 9?
items.e: Count back 1: 9, 8. One less is the number just before.

items.q: What is one more than 13?
items.e: Count on 1: 13, 14. Only the ones digit changes.

items.q: What is one less than 18?
items.e: Count back 1: 18, 17. One less is the number just before.

items.q: What is one more than 19?
items.e: Count on 1: 19, 20. After 9 ones comes a new ten.

items.q: What is one less than 20?
items.e: Count back 1: 20, 19. Do not jump back a whole ten.

items.q: What is one more than 34?
items.e: Count on 1: 34, 35. Only the ones digit changes.

items.q: What is one less than 47?
items.e: Count back 1: 47, 46. One less is the number just before.

items.q: What is one more than 29?
items.e: Count on 1: 29, 30. After 9 ones comes a new ten.

items.q: What is one less than 40?
items.e: Count back 1: 40, 39. Do not jump back a whole ten.

items.q: What is one more than 59?
items.e: Count on 1: 59, 60. After 9 ones comes a new ten.

items.q: What is one less than 71?
items.e: Count back 1: 71, 70. One less is the number just before.

items.q: What is one more than 66?
items.e: Count on 1: 66, 67. Only the ones digit changes.

items.q: What is one less than 30?
items.e: Count back 1: 30, 29. Do not jump back a whole ten.

items.q: What is one more than 89?
items.e: Count on 1: 89, 90. After 9 ones comes a new ten.

items.q: What is one less than 52?
items.e: Count back 1: 52, 51. One less is the number just before.

items.q: What is one more than 99?
items.e: Count on 1: 99, 100. Ten tens make one hundred.

items.q: What is one less than 100?
items.e: Count back 1: 100, 99. Do not jump back a whole ten.

items.q: What is one less than 80?
items.e: Count back 1: 80, 79. Do not jump back a whole ten.

items.q: What is one more than 45?
items.e: Count on 1: 45, 46. Only the ones digit changes.

sets.title: Count forwards and backwards across tens

items.q: Count on: 0, 1, 2, 3, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Count on 1 from 3. After 3 comes 4.

items.q: Count back: 5, 4, 3, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Count back 1 from 3. Before 3 comes 2.

items.q: This is part of a hundred square. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: Just left of the ? is 4. Count on 1. The ? is 5.

items.q: This is part of a hundred square. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: Just left of the ? is 18. Count on 1. The ? is 19.

items.q: Count on: 27, 28, 29, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: After 29 comes 30. 9 ones and 1 more make a new ten. Do not write 210.

items.q: Count back: 23, 22, 21, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Count back 1 from 21. Before 21 comes 20.

items.q: This is part of a hundred square. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: Count on: 27, 28, 29, 30. A row of the square ends with a ten.

items.q: Count on: 47, 48, 49, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: After 49 comes 50. 4 tens become 5 tens. Do not go back to 40.

items.q: This is part of a hundred square. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: Just right of the ? is 56. Count back 1. The ? is 55.

items.q: Count back: 42, 41, 40, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Count back 1 from 40. Before 40 comes 39. 49 is wrong: 40 − 1 goes down a ten.

items.q: Count on: 68, 69, ☐, 71. What number goes in the box?
items.e: After 69 comes 70, then 71.

items.q: This is part of a hundred square. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: Just left of the ? is 69. Count on 1. The ? is 70.

items.q: Count back: 72, 71, 70, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Count back 1 from 70. Before 70 comes 69. Not 79.

items.q: This is part of a hundred square. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: Count on: 87, 88, 89, 90. Or look up: 80 and one row down is 90.

items.q: Count back: 62, ☐, 60, 59. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Counting back: 62, 61, 60, 59.

items.q: This is part of a hundred square. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: Just above the ? is 81. One row down is 10 more. The ? is 91.

items.q: This is part of a hundred square. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: Just above the ? is 45. One row down is 10 more. The ? is 55.

items.q: Count on: 97, 98, 99, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: After 99 comes 100. Ten tens make one hundred.

items.q: Count back: 100, 99, ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Count back 1 from 99. Before 99 comes 98.

items.q: This is part of a hundred square. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: Count on: 97, 98, 99, 100. 100 is the last box on the square.

sets.title: More, less, fewer, most and least

items.q: Which row has the most counters?
items.e: Count each row: A has 4, B has 6, C has 3, D has 8. Row D has 8. That is the most.
Count each row: A has 7, B has 5, C has 9, D has 6. Row B has 5. That is the fewest.

items.q: Which number is the arrow pointing to?
items.e: Find 5. Count the small marks to the right: 6, 7. The arrow is at 7.

items.q: Which row has 7 balls?
items.e: Count each row: A has 12, B has 9, C has 11, D has 7. Row D has 7. It is equal to 7.

items.q: Which number is the arrow pointing to?
items.e: Find 5. Count the small marks to the left: 4. The arrow is at 4.

items.q: Which row has the most apples?
items.e: Count each row: A has 9, B has 10, C has 12, D has 8. Row C has 12. That is the most.

items.q: Which number is the arrow pointing to?
items.e: Find 15. Count the small marks to the left: 14, 13. The arrow is at 13.
Count each row: A has 8, B has 10, C has 6, D has 9. Row B has 10. It is equal to 10.

items.q: Which row has the fewest counters?
items.e: Count each row: A has 11, B has 13, C has 15, D has 14. Row A has 11. That is the fewest.

items.q: Which number is the arrow pointing to?
items.e: Find 15. Count the small marks to the right: 16, 17, 18. The arrow is at 18.
Count each row: A has 14, B has 11, C has 12, D has 13. Row A has 14. That is the most.

items.q: Which row has the fewest balls?
items.e: Count each row: A has 14, B has 15, C has 12, D has 13. Row C has 12. That is the fewest.

items.q: Which number is more than 36?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 41 has 4 tens. 36 has 3 tens. So 41 is more. 29 has 9 ones, but only 2 tens.

items.q: Which number is less than 52?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 25 has 2 tens. 52 has 5 tens. So 25 is less. 52 is equal, not less.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. 41 is 4 tens and 1 one. So 14 is less than 41.

items.q: Which number is the greatest: 38, 83, 47, 74?
items.e: Look at the tens. 83 has 8 tens. That is the most tens. 83 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least: 45, 54, 40, 50?
items.e: 45 and 40 have the fewest tens: 4 tens. 40 has 0 ones. 40 is the least.

items.q: Mohammed has 12 sweets. Amelia has 9. Jack has 15. George has 11. Who has the fewest?
items.e: 9 is the smallest number. Amelia has the fewest sweets.

items.q: Which number is more than 69 and less than 72?
items.e: Count on from 69: 70, 71, 72. 70 is more than 69 and less than 72. 72 is not less than 72.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Count on: 59, 60. 60 comes after 59. So 60 is more than 59.

items.q: It is Maya’s birthday. How old is she?
items.e: Count the candles. Touch each one once: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. She is 6.

items.q: Ruby has a candle for each year. How old is she?
items.e: Count the candles once each: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. She is 7.

items.q: Ethan is 6 today. How old will he be next birthday?
items.e: Next birthday is one more year. One more than 6 is 7.

items.q: Alfie walks up these steps. How many steps are there?
items.e: Count each step once: 1, 2, 3 … 10, 11, 12. There are 12 steps.

items.q: Maya swims 17 lengths. Then she swims 1 more. How many lengths?
items.e: One more than 17 is 18.

items.q: How many cars are in the car park?
items.e: Count across the top row: 7 cars. Count on along the bottom row: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. There are 14 cars.

items.q: How many empty spaces are there?
items.e: Count only the empty spaces, not the cars. Top row: 3. Bottom row: 3. 3 and 3 is 6.

items.q: One more car parks. How many cars will there be?
items.e: There are 19 cars. One more than 19 is 20. Now the car park is full.

items.q: Noah’s coat peg is number 19. The next peg is one more. What number is it?
items.e: One more than 19 is 20. 9 ones and 1 more make 2 tens.

items.q: There are 29 children in Class 1. One more child joins. How many now?
items.e: One more than 29 is 30. Do not write 210.

items.q: Isla counts buttons in a jar: 37, 38, 39. What comes next?
items.e: After 39 comes 40. 9 ones and 1 more make a new ten.

items.q: Oliver has 74 stickers. He gives 1 away. How many are left?
items.e: One less than 74 is 73. 75 would be one more.

items.q: Poppy is on page 60. She turns back 1 page. What page is she on?
items.e: One less than 60 is 59. Not 69: going back 1 from 60 goes down to 5 tens.

items.q: The bus has 50 people on it. 1 gets off. How many are on the bus now?
items.e: One less than 50 is 49. Not 40: that is 10 less.

items.q: Jack walks down 20 steps. He counts back: 20, 19, 18 … What comes after 11?
items.e: Counting back, the number after 11 is 10.

items.q: Freya counts back for hide and seek: 100, 99, 98, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Count back 1 from 98. Next is 97.

items.q: At lunchtime Leo has 15 grapes. Aisha has 18. Lily has 12. Charlie has 16. Who has the most?
items.e: 18 is the biggest number. Aisha has the most grapes.

items.q: Raffle tickets go 87, 88, 89 … Ruby gets the next one. What number is it?
items.e: After 89 comes 90. 8 tens become 9 tens.

items.q: Class 1 has a star chart. Harry has 31 stars. Evie has 13. Mohammed has 30. Amelia has 21. Who has the least?
items.e: 13 has only 1 ten. That is the fewest tens. Evie has the least.

items.q: George has 3 packs of 10 pencils and 4 more pencils. How many pencils?
